complexity_scope.guarantee: Expectation over stochastic rewards at each fixed horizon, uniformly in the sense that the same bound applies for every horizon; no simultaneous sample-path probability claim.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Displayed constants are explicit: 8 and 1+pi^2/3; gap dependence is explicitly shown.
complexity_scope.oracle: One reward from the chosen arm's next sample per play.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Sequential arm choices; expected cumulative regret R_n, not realized-regret concentration or a terminal recommendation error.
complexity_scope.regime: Independent stationary arm rewards supported in [0,1]; any integer K>1 and any integer n>=1.
complexity_scope.resource: n total arm plays, including initialization. Arithmetic, storage and bit costs are not bounded by this theorem.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Upper performance bound for selected Figure 1 UCB1 only; no unrestricted-policy lower bound or unrestricted Oracle Complexity characterization.

issues.description: Printed infinite-sum extension and subsequent finite-horizon threshold explanation require the finite-time interpretation recorded in the Proof map. No local correction theorem is asserted.

evidence.statement_check: Theorem 1 formula visually checked on PDF p.3 against standing assumptions and definitions on pp.1–3; source Proof read on pp.8–9.

content.intended_use: Control finite-time expected cumulative regret of Figure 1 UCB1.

dependencies: Within-source Fact 1, PDF p.8 / p.242; reward assumptions, PDF pp.1–2; Figure 1, PDF p.3.
proofs.locator: PDF pp.8–9 / journal pp.242–243, Proof of Theorem 1, equations (6)–(9); Fact 1 on p.242
map: At p.242 set c_{t,s}=sqrt(2 ln(t)/s). Equation (6) bounds the number of suboptimal-arm plays by a threshold ell plus a sum of index-comparison indicators over time and fixed prefix counts.
Equations (7)–(9): an index comparison implies either a downward deviation of an optimal-arm mean, an upward deviation of the suboptimal-arm mean, or mu*<mu_i+2c_{t,s_i}.
Fact 1 bounds each fixed-prefix deviation probability by t^-4. Choose ell=ceil(8 ln(n)/Delta_i^2). For original finite times t<=n and s_i>=ell, the third event is impossible.
On p.243 sum the remaining tail probabilities to obtain E[T_i(n)]<=8 ln(n)/Delta_i^2+1+pi^2/3; multiplying by each positive gap and summing gives the displayed regret bound.
proofs.omitted_details: Faithful source Proof map, not a local independent Proof certificate. The printed derivation extends a sum to infinity before asserting event (9) is impossible using ln(n); that impossibility applies to the original finite time range. The map records the finite-time interpretation rather than silently treating the printed infinite-range assertion as literal.
proofs.reading_coverage: Actually viewed PDF-page JPEGs 8 and 9, including Fact 1, equations (6)–(9), the two t^-4 bounds, threshold and final count estimate; also viewed statement and policy on PDF p.3. No independent reproof or Reviewer acceptance claimed.

assumptions: For every arm i, X_{i,1},X_{i,2},... are iid with unknown law P_i supported in [0,1]. Rewards across different arms are independent, as specified in the Introduction.
Run Figure 1 UCB1: play each arm once; after m completed plays choose a maximizer of the empirical mean plus sqrt(2 ln(m)/T_i(m)), observing and updating only the selected arm.
statement.conclusion: R_n <= 8 sum_{i:mu_i<mu*} ln(n)/Delta_i + (1+pi^2/3) sum_{j=1}^K Delta_j. Empty reciprocal-gap sums are zero.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Arm i has rewards X_{i,s}, indexed by its own play count s, and mean mu_i. Let T_i(n) count plays of i among the first n total plays; mu*=max_i mu_i, Delta_i=mu*-mu_i, and R_n=n mu* - sum_i mu_i E[T_i(n)]. Natural logarithms are used.
statement.parameter_domains: K is an integer >=2; n is an integer >=1. Means lie in [0,1], Delta_i in [0,1]; denominators involve only Delta_i>0. For n<K the policy is truncated during its one-play-per-arm initialization; the source states any number n of plays, whereas its displayed main counting Proof is written after initialization.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every integer K>1 and every collection of reward laws satisfying these assumptions, the stated expected regret bound holds at every fixed integer horizon n>=1. Expectation is over the rewards. No unique optimal arm or positive minimum gap is assumed; only strictly suboptimal arms enter the reciprocal-gap sum.
